title: Formal smoothness for an adic topology is stable under base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal such that $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $R\to R'$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings, $S'=S\otimes_RR'$ [def-weil-module-base-change] (a commutative ring, and an $R'$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] via $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$) and $\mathfrak n'=\mathfrak nS'$ the ideal of $S'$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak n$ under $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Then $S'$ is formally smooth over $R'$ for the $\mathfrak n'$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, line 9346) and its proof (universal property of the tensor product)

proof.text: Unfold the lifting definition, introduce a square-zero lifting problem, and install the scalar-tower algebra structures induced by R → R' → D and its quotient. Restrict the given map along includeLeft.
The image of n^k under includeLeft lies in the kth power of the mapped ideal, by Ideal.map_pow and Ideal.mem_map_of_mem, so the restricted map kills n^k.
Apply the universe-polymorphic lifting bridge to obtain an R-algebra lift f:S→D.
Use Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap with f and the R-algebra restriction of the R'-structure map on D; package the resulting ring hom as an R'-algebra hom by checking its scalar commutation.

The quotient composites agree on both tensor inclusions (the left one by the lift equation and the right one by commutation with algebra maps); Algebra.TensorProduct.ext gives equality, hence the constructed map lifts the original map.

split_report.summary: Proof written from Stacks More on Algebra 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, line 9346; tag checked in tags/tags) and its three-sentence proof, against the DAG definition def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic exactly (commutative D with a ring map, J^2 = 0, g(n^k) = 0 for some k ≥ 1). Five steps: (1) the lifting problem over R' and the restricted R-algebra map g = g'∘ι; (2) ι(n^k) ⊆ n'^k, so g kills n^k (elementary); (3) the lift f:S → D from the hypothesis; (4) the R'-algebra map f':S⊗R' → D from f and ρ:R' → D by the pushout property of the tensor product; (5) q∘f' = g' by the uniqueness clause (Stacks leaves this implicit). The existing node lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property puts the base ring on the left (S ⊗_R A, S-algebra maps) and would need the swap S⊗R' ≅ R'⊗S; it also gives no ring structure. So one new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property (ring structure on A⊗_R B, existence of h(a⊗b)=f(a)g(b), uniqueness; Algebra.TensorProduct.instCommRing/productMap/ext) was created and added to stmt_deps, since the statement's 'S' is a commutative ring and an R'-algebra' uses its clause (1).
